es-republic.title: Flag of the Second Spanish Republic

colors.note: Represents the people of Castile (pendón morado).

desc:
- The flag of the Spanish Republic (1931–1939) was a red, yellow, and purple horizontal tricolour, replacing the traditional red-yellow-red of the monarchy with a purple band at the bottom
- The purple stripe (morado) was believed to represent the people of Castile and the Comuneros revolt
- The Second Republic's flag is still used today by Spanish republicans and left-wing movements
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands of red (top), yellow, and purple (Tyrian purple)
- The coat of arms with a mural crown sits centred
- Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- The Spanish Republic flag (1931–1939) represented democratic Spain
- Overthrown by Franco during the Spanish Civil War
- The purple stripe (rarely used) represented historical Castile

es-francoist.title: Flag of Francoist Spain
desc:
- The flag of Francoist Spain (1945–1977) was the red-yellow-red bicolour with the Francoist coat of arms — the eagle of St John holding the yoke and arrows of the Catholic Monarchs
- Used during Francisco Franco's dictatorship, this flag combined traditional Spanish colours with symbols of the authoritarian regime
- The eagle was removed after the transition to democracy
- **Construction:** three horizontal stripes in ratio 1:2:1 (red-yellow-red). The Francoist coat of arms centred on the yellow stripe. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- The Francoist flag (1936–1975) represented Spain under Franco's authoritarian rule
- The eagle represented Francoist ideology and fascism
- Spain transitioned to democracy after Franco's death

es-empire.title: Flag of the Spanish Empire (Cross of Burgundy)
desc: - The Spanish Empire used the Cross of Burgundy (Cruz de Borgoña) — a red ragged saltire on white — from the 16th to 18th centuries across its global territories
- **Construction:** a red field (often burgundy cross or the Cross of Burgundy, a red ragged saltire on white)
trivia:
- The Spanish Empire flag represented one of history's largest global empires
- Spain controlled vast territories across the Americas, Africa, and Asia
- The empire lasted from 1492 (Columbus) to the 20th century
